question: A pill cuts a disease's yearly risk from 2 in 1,000 to 1 in 1,000. How many must take it to spare one person?
answer: About 1,000. The pill halves the risk, but the risk was 2 in 1,000 to begin with, so it removes one case per 1,000 people a year. Doctors call this the number needed to treat. The same halving on a 1-in-2 risk would spare one person in four.
move: Ask what a halving is a halving of before you are impressed.
trap: Hearing that the pill halves the risk and picturing half the patients saved.
reference: Laupacis, Sackett & Roberts, An assessment of clinically useful measures of the consequences of treatment, New England Journal of Medicine, 1988
